turns.text: Hi, I need to move my cardiology visit to Friday if possible. My daughter drives me to all my appointments, and she can only do mornings because she works afternoons.
I can help with that. I will look for a Friday morning cardiology slot and confirm it with you before I change anything.
Also I weighed myself today and I have put on 2.5 kg since Sunday. I take furosemide 40 mg every morning, by the way.
Thank you for telling me about the weight gain. That is something a nurse should know about today, so I am creating an urgent task for a nurse coordinator to call you.

Thanks. Another thing I wanted to understand better is how long I should keep walking each day now that I am home. The discharge papers mention walking but I could not remember whether it was ten minutes or twenty, and whether I should do it all at once or split it across the morning and evening when it is cooler outside.

Your care plan describes the walking routine your team set for you. I can read it out exactly as written. In general the plan's instructions are the ones to follow, and if anything feels unclear or you are not sure it still applies to you, I can ask a nurse coordinator to call you and go through it.

That makes sense. Could you also remind me what the clinic hours are for the outpatient building, and whether there is a separate entrance for people coming for follow-up visits? Last time I went in through the emergency side by mistake and it took a long time to find the right desk.

Outpatient follow-up visits use the main outpatient entrance, not the emergency entrance. When you arrive, the reception desk on the ground floor checks you in and tells you which clinic room to go to. I can include these directions when I confirm any appointment for you.

Good. What should I bring with me to the appointment? I have a folder with my discharge summary, a list of the questions I wrote down, and my insurance card, but I am not sure if they need anything else from me on the day of the visit or if I should come early to fill in forms.

Bringing your discharge summary and your list of questions is a good idea. Plan to arrive about fifteen minutes early so the front desk can check you in. If the clinic needs any other paperwork, they will tell you at check-in, and I can pass on any specific requests from the clinic before your visit.

Okay. And is parking available near the outpatient building? Whoever brings me usually drops me off first and then parks, but last time the car park was full and they had to drive around for a while. I would like to tell them what to expect this time so we are not late.

There is a visitor car park next to the outpatient building, and it is usually busiest in the late morning. Dropping you at the entrance first is a good plan. I will mention parking in the appointment confirmation so the person driving you knows where to go.

One more general question. If I need to talk to someone about my follow-up plan outside of this chat, who do I contact? I do not want to call the ward every time, and I am never sure whether my question is important enough to bother a nurse with.

You can always message here, and when something needs a person, I create a task for a nurse coordinator, who will contact you. Questions about your follow-up plan are never a bother. If anything feels urgent, call your care team directly, and in an emergency call 112.

Thank you, that is reassuring. I also wanted to check whether the follow-up visits can be done by video instead of in person, because some days it is hard for me to travel, especially when the weather is bad or when the person who usually helps me is busy at work.

Your care plan lists the follow-up visits your team wants, and some of them need to be in person so they can examine you. If you would like to ask whether a particular visit could be done by video, I can create a request for the coordinator to check with the clinic.

I see. How will I know that an appointment has really been booked? Last time I thought something was booked over the phone, but when I arrived the clinic had no record of it and I had to wait a long time to be squeezed in between other patients, which was very tiring.

When I book or change an appointment, I only do it after you confirm, and then I tell you the date, time, clinic and the name of the clinician. That booking is recorded in the hospital's appointment system straight away, so the clinic sees the same details you do.

That is good to hear. What happens if I am running late on the day? Sometimes the traffic near the hospital is terrible in the mornings, and I worry that if I arrive ten or fifteen minutes late they will cancel my visit and I will have to start all over again.

If you are running late, it is best to call the clinic reception so they know you are on your way. Clinics usually try to fit you in if they know to expect you. If a visit does get missed, message me and I can help you find a new slot within your care plan.

Alright. Can I see a list of everything that is planned for me over the next few weeks in one place? I keep losing track of which visits and tests are still coming up and which ones are already done, and the paper copy from the ward is getting crumpled.

Yes. I can list your booked appointments at any time, and I can read out the follow-up items in your care plan with their due dates. That way you can see what is already booked and what still needs a booking, and I can help you book the rest.

Thank you. Lastly, is there a cafeteria or somewhere to sit near the outpatient clinics? If I have more than one appointment on the same day there might be a long gap in between, and I get tired quickly if I have to stand or walk around for too long.

There is a cafeteria on the ground floor of the outpatient building with seating, and there are waiting areas outside each clinic. If you have two visits on the same day, I can try to book them close together to keep the gap short when slots allow.

Okay, one really last thing. Will I get a reminder before each appointment? I am worried I will forget, because there are so many different visits and tests in these few weeks and my memory has not been great since I came home from the hospital.

Yes. After a booking is confirmed, the clinic sends a reminder before the visit using the contact details on your record. You can also ask me at any time what is coming up next, and I will list your upcoming appointments with their dates and times.
My oxygen reading this morning was 91 on the finger monitor. Please only phone me after 6 pm, I do not read texts or emails.
Thank you. I have noted that phone calls after 6 pm work best for you. I will pass your oxygen reading to a nurse coordinator.
I use a wheelchair now, so I need a clinic room that is wheelchair accessible. And my inhaler seems to be running out faster than before.
I will make sure the clinic knows you need a wheelchair-accessible room. A nurse coordinator will follow up about your inhaler.
